20 A scientist is investigating the properties of a new material. She plots a force-extension graph for
the material up to its breaking point.
R
force
Q
P
0
0
extension
Which statement must be correct?
A
The area under the graph from P to R is the strain energy stored in the material.
B
The area under the graph from P to R is the work done in stretching the material.
C
The material stretches elastically from Q to R.
D
The material stretches plastically from P to Q.

hints: Look at the shape from P to Q to R: P to Q is straight through the origin and Q is the bend where the gradient falls toward R.
Recall that work done in stretching is $area$ under the force against extension in $\text{N}$ against $\text{m}$, while stored strain energy is only the recoverable part.
Ask whether the material would return to zero extension if unloaded from beyond Q, and what that implies for stored energy versus total work.
walkthrough: Identify the graph features: force on the y-axis against extension on the x-axis, with a linear section P to Q followed by a less steep section Q to R up to breaking.
State the governing rule: small element of work is $dW = F \, dx$, so total work done is $W = \text{area under force-extension graph}$ from zero to maximum extension.
Apply it to P to R: the whole area under the curve from P to R therefore equals the work done by the stretching force, whether deformation is elastic or plastic.

Distinguish strain energy: stored elastic strain energy equals work done only while deformation is elastic; beyond the elastic limit at Q some work is used for permanent plastic flow and dissipated as heat.
Identify the limit: the bend at Q is the elastic limit, so P to Q is elastic and Q to R is mainly plastic, which reverses options C and D.
Therefore the statement that must hold for any such curve is that area from P to R is work done. This is option B.

A.explanation: Not all the work done is stored as recoverable strain energy once plastic deformation occurs after Q, so some energy is dissipated.

B.explanation: Total work done to stretch is always $W = \int F \, dx$, which is the total area under the force-extension curve from P to R.

C.explanation: The kink at Q marks the elastic limit, so Q to R with reduced gradient is plastic stretching, not reversible elastic stretching.

D.explanation: P to Q is straight and through the origin, showing proportional elastic behaviour obeying Hooke's law, not permanent plastic stretching.
